speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; to determine the cause, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and has your stool turned black or bloody?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Malrotation with Midgut Volvulus.

The clinical presentation of bilious vomiting in a newborn born six hours after delivery is a surgical emergency; the history of a sibling with pyloric stenosis does not explain the bilious nature of the emesis. I am requesting an Emergent Upper GI Series to confirm the diagnosis and rule out malrotation.
